problem: Britannica calls the Lysicrates monument the first known use of Corinthian capitals on the outside of a building, not the earliest surviving Corinthian columns. Earlier Corinthian columns stood inside buildings: the temple of Apollo at Bassae (late 5th century BCE) and the tholoi at Delphi and Epidaurus, whose fragments survive.
proposed: The Monument of Lysicrates in Athens, built in 334 BCE to celebrate a victory at the City Dionysia, is the first known building with Corinthian columns on its outside; earlier ones stood inside temples.
evidence: Britannica: 'The first known use of a Corinthian capital on the outside of a building is that of the choragic Monument of Lysicrates (Athens, 335/334 bc).' Earlier interior Corinthian capitals are known from Bassae and the Epidaurus tholos.
